prompt: When is the bare prompt's prose reply good enough as it is?
hint: Who reads it next?

choices.text: When a person reads it
choices.why: Right: `Shipping` and `urgent` are fine for a person.

choices.text: Only in a demo
choices.why: A person on the team reads prose fine in production too.

choices.text: Never, since structured output is more reliable than prose for any reader at all
choices.why: Structure is for a program; a person gains nothing from braces.

choices.text: When the model is told to be friendly and professional
choices.why: Tone has nothing to do with who consumes the answer.

prompt: The mean reply was 22.7 tokens under `v1-bare.txt` and 39.9 under `v2-json.txt`. How many more output tokens does an average JSON reply carry?
hint: Subtract.

prompt: Why is JSON the wrong format for a note that a person will read and judge?
hint: Two costs are named.

choices.text: Every field takes a decision away from the model, and the braces cost tokens the person gets nothing from
choices.why: Right: constraint and cost, for a reader who needed neither.

choices.text: JSON cannot hold sentences
choices.why: The summary field holds one.

choices.text: People cannot read JSON
choices.why: They can; it just adds nothing for them.

choices.text: The model refuses to write it
choices.why: Twenty-seven of forty parsed under `v2-json.txt`.

prompt: Between them, what do the `fields` and `labels` checks require of a reply?
hint: The three things a JSON schema says most often.

choices.text: That the summary is accurate, short and free of the customer's name and email address
choices.why: Neither check reads the summary's content.

choices.text: Required keys, allowed keys and allowed values
choices.why: Right: a schema in miniature.

choices.text: The person's labels
choices.why: That is `category` and `urgency`.

choices.text: Parse, retry, route
choices.why: Those are things the consuming program does.

prompt: A reply is a JSON object with `category` and `urgency`, both from the lists, and no `summary`. Does it pass `fields`?
hint: Read which keys the check requires.

choices.text: No: the prompt asks for three fields, so the check requires three
choices.why: The check is not a copy of the prompt; it requires two.

choices.text: No, it is rejected as `missing summary`
choices.why: Only `category` and `urgency` can be missing.

choices.text: Only if a `confidence` key is there instead
choices.why: `confidence` is allowed, not required.

choices.text: Yes
choices.why: Right: the router needs two keys, and the check asks for those.

prompt: Which of the five checks can the consuming program run on a reply in production?
hint: What does a production message not have yet?

choices.text: `json`, `fields` and `labels`, since the other two need a person's answer for that message
choices.why: Right: the format can be checked on every call.

choices.text: The five of them
choices.why: Nobody has labelled a production message yet.

choices.text: `category` and `urgency`
choices.why: Those are exactly the two that need a label.

choices.text: Not one, until a person labels it
choices.why: The format checks need no label.

prompt: The format can be verified on every call; the content can only be ___.
hint: On a test set, with a person's labels.

prompt: In the stand-in, what did adding *Reply with only the JSON object: no code fence and no other text* do?
hint: Three replies still came back wrapped.

choices.text: Removed every code fence and preamble from all forty replies
choices.why: Three of forty were still wrapped.

choices.text: Changed the categories the model chose for most messages
choices.why: The categories were unchanged; the wrapping changed.

choices.text: Made the wrapping rarer, not gone
choices.why: Right: 37 of 40 parse, against 27.

choices.text: A change too small to measure
choices.why: The sign test gave p = 0.006.

prompt: Under `v4-only-json.txt`, checked strictly, how many of the forty replies parse?
hint: The `json` row of `pl check`.

prompt: Under `--lenient`, `v2-json.txt` and `v4-only-json.txt` both parse forty of forty. Why is that a problem for you?
hint: What did the strict check see that this one does not?

choices.text: Because the lenient parser crashes on code fences and then counts each of those crashes as a reply that passed
choices.why: It does not crash; it cuts the object out and parses that.

choices.text: It hides the improvement the strict check measured, so the line's effect is invisible
choices.why: Right: p = 0.006 under strict, no difference under lenient.

choices.text: It makes the prompts slower
choices.why: Parsing does not touch the model call.

choices.text: Nothing: 40 of 40 is the goal
choices.why: The goal is a measurement that sees the format.

prompt: Your program has to accept replies inside a code fence. Where does the step that strips the fence belong?
hint: Keep the measurement able to see it.

choices.text: Inside the check, so the measurement ignores fences that do not matter
choices.why: Then the check can no longer see what is being repaired.

choices.text: In the prompt, as a paragraph asking the model to repair its own reply
choices.why: The prompt already asks for no fence; the repair is for when it is ignored.

choices.text: In the test set, beside each expected answer
choices.why: The test set holds labels, not code.

choices.text: In the consuming program, counted
choices.why: Right: a named step, and a count that warns when it climbs.

prompt: Which of these replies would the lenient parser accept as JSON? Choose all that apply.
hint: It takes everything from the first `{` to the last `}`.

choices.text: An object inside a code fence
choices.why: Yes: the fence is outside the braces.

choices.text: A sentence, then an object
choices.why: Yes: the sentence is cut away.

choices.text: A paragraph of apology with an object in the middle of it
choices.why: Yes, and that is why it cannot tell a habit from a different answer.

choices.text: Plain prose with no braces in it
choices.why: There is no object to cut out.

prompt: Three samples per message at temperature 0, and the same three messages failed to parse every time. Why, in the stand-in?
hint: What decides a habit there?

choices.text: A habit is decided by the prompt and the message, so asking again asks the same question
choices.why: Right: nothing changed between the calls.

choices.text: The harness caches failed replies
choices.why: No cache is on; each call is made.

choices.text: The model was down
choices.why: It answered all 120 calls.

choices.text: Three samples is too few
choices.why: More of the same would fail the same way.

prompt: Why is a message in the wrong queue worse than one sent to the unsorted queue?
hint: Both are late.

choices.text: The unsorted queue is answered first, because the support team gives it priority every morning
choices.why: The lesson says nothing about its priority.

choices.text: It is late and also lost among somebody else's work
choices.why: Right: the unsorted one is only late.

choices.text: It costs more tokens
choices.why: Routing costs no tokens.

choices.text: Wrong queues delete messages
choices.why: Nothing is deleted.

prompt: Which failure does a provider's structured-output mode leave in place?
hint: It constrains the format.

choices.text: A sentence placed in front of the object by habit
choices.why: That is a format failure, which the mode prevents.

choices.text: A code fence wrapped around the whole reply
choices.why: Also format; also prevented.

choices.text: A wrong category in valid JSON
choices.why: Right: it constrains the format and not the answer.

choices.text: A missing brace
choices.why: Valid JSON has its braces.

prompt: What is wrong with searching an unparseable reply for `billing` and routing on what you find?
hint: Who checked the decision?

choices.text: It is too slow for a pipeline handling a thousand messages a day
choices.why: Speed is not the problem; nobody checks what it decides.

choices.text: Regular expressions cannot match words inside JSON text
choices.why: They can; that is not the objection.

choices.text: It needs a second model call to do the search
choices.why: A search needs no model.

choices.text: It is an unchecked guess
choices.why: Right: a format failure turned into a content decision.

prompt: Three replies in forty did not parse. At that rate, about how many replies a day would a router fail to read out of a thousand messages?
Put what the consuming program does with a reply in order.
hint: The repair comes before the parse.

prompt: Match each thing to where it runs.
hint: Production has no person's labels.

pairs.right: On a test set with a person's answers

pairs.left: A step that strips code fences
pairs.right: In the consuming program, with a count

prompt: A colleague sees forty of forty parse with `--lenient` and proposes deleting the line *Reply with only the JSON object* to shorten the prompt. What do you ask to see first?
hint: Which parser can see what the line does?

choices.text: A lenient run of the shorter prompt over the holdout set too, to be sure across seventy messages instead of forty
choices.why: More lenient numbers still cannot see the wrapping.

choices.text: The strict count with and without the line, compared message by message
choices.why: Right: only the strict check measured that line, at p = 0.006.

choices.text: Forty of forty settles it
choices.why: Lenient numbers hide exactly what the line fixed.

choices.text: A run at a higher temperature
choices.why: Temperature is beside the point here.
